claims.claim: The US–Canada treaty lets Canada credit US estate tax on US property and the US credit Canada's tax at death on non-US property

sources.name: Finance Canada: Canada–US tax convention (consolidated), Article XXIX B (read from offset 100,000)
sources.says: Art. XXIX B(6): Canada allows US federal and state estate and inheritance taxes on property situated in the US "as a deduction from the amount of any Canadian tax otherwise payable" on income arising in the US. Art. XXIX B(7): for a US citizen or resident, the US allows "a credit ... against such tax imposed in respect of property situated outside the United States" for Canadian income taxes arising from the death.

sources.name: IRS: Estate & gift tax treaties (international)
sources.says: All 13 countries are in the table (see us-estate-treaty-list). Estate & Gift: Australia, Austria, France, Germany, Japan, United Kingdom. Estate only: Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, South Africa, Switzerland, and Canada by Article XXIX B of the income tax treaty.

claims.note: The IRS list (shared) confirms an estate provision in the income tax treaty; what it does was read in Art. XXIX B(6)–(7). Canada's relief is a deduction against Canadian tax on US-source income, which the profiles call a credit.
